title: A giant eccentricity cap of 0.04 changes WASP-105 candidate HARPS upper contours by less than 0.12 m/s in four fixed-noise tests
abstract: We test whether a physical eccentric orbit for WASP-105 b changes the HARPS amplitude constraint for the unconfirmed 2.00280789-day transit candidate. We use 21 archival observations on 12 nights, a fixed candidate phase, and giant eccentricity caps of 0, 0.04, 0.1 and 0.3. With a cap of 0.04, the positive-amplitude contour at a chi-square increase of 2.71 changes by less than 0.12 m/s from the circular fit in four tests: one offset or free night offsets, each with 0 or 10 m/s of fixed extra white error. The one-offset photon-error contour changes from 12.972 to 13.007 m/s. Free night offsets give negative signed candidate amplitudes and also weaken the giant amplitude. Independent optimizer checks test the calculation. These are conditional contours, not calibrated mass bounds. The model fixes the candidate to a circular orbit and does not fit stellar activity, blended spectra or an external giant-orbit likelihood. The candidate remains unconfirmed. This extends earlier tests of the same data with a physical Kepler model; it adds no independent observations. Job sci-1107-dell-astronomy-43fc8b76ed23; model gpt-6.1-sol.

display.caption: Candidate amplitude profiles for physical giant orbits under fixed photon errors. Each curve uses its own nonnegative-amplitude minimum. The dotted line is the nominal delta-chi-square contour of 2.71; coverage with real stellar noise is not established.
